description: Data type for the sparse-attention indexer K cache. "auto" picks the model's default (bf16 for MiniMax M3, fp8 for the DeepSeek sparse indexer). Quantized formats (fp8, mxfp4, nvfp4) require indexer kernel support in the backend.

name: attention.hisparse_config.device_buffer_size
description: Total per-request GPU hot-buffer rows, including the newest-token slot. Defaults to one top-k per decode query plus one top-k of LRU slack. The physical allocation is rounded up to the GPU cache block size selected from the active backends.

name: attention.hisparse_config.eager_host_mirror
description: Mirror decode-written KV rows to the host pool during the forward so page spills complete without moving data. When disabled, decode rows stay resident-only and evicted pages are copied to host at spill time. Prefill rows are always mirrored during the forward.

name: attention.use_non_causal
description: Whether to use non-causal (bidirectional) attention.

name: attention.sparse_mla_force_mqa
description: Force sparse MLA to use forward_mqa for all requests, including prefill. When False (default), pure prefill batches use forward_mha when implemented. Set to True to always use the MQA path.

name: attention.flex_attn_block_m
description: Triton kernel BLOCK_M tile size for flex attention. Must be a power of 2 >= 16. If None and VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1, defaults to 16.

name: attention.flex_attn_block_n
description: Triton kernel BLOCK_N tile size for flex attention. Must be a power of 2 >= 16. If None and VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1, defaults to 16.

name: attention.flex_attn_q_block_size
description: Logical Q block size for the flex attention block mask. Must be a power of 2 and divisible by flex_attn_block_m. If None, uses 16 for paged KV attention on PyTorch >= 2.9, and 128 for encoder-only attention or older PyTorch versions.

name: attention.flex_attn_kv_block_size
description: Logical KV block size for the flex attention block mask. Must be a power of 2 and divisible by flex_attn_block_n. If None, uses the KV cache block size for paged KV attention on PyTorch >= 2.9, and 128 for encoder-only attention or older PyTorch versions.

name: engram.cpu_offload
description: Store embedding weights in pinned CPU memory for UVA lookup. Defaults to VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD, which is enabled by default. An explicit value takes precedence over the environment variable.

name: engram.embedding_across_dp
description: Shard embeddings across TP and all DP ranks when enabled. Otherwise, each DP rank has a separate TP-sharded embedding replica.

name: engram.dp_shared_memory
description: Share CPU-offloaded embedding weights between co-located DP replicas. Each node stores one copy of every TP shard, reducing host memory without per-step Engram DP collectives. Requires sufficient /dev/shm capacity and a shared IPC namespace.

name: reasoning.reasoning_parser
description: The name of the ReasoningParser to use for this model.

name: reasoning.reasoning_start_str
description: String that indicates the start of reasoning.

name: reasoning.reasoning_end_str
description: String forced when the thinking budget is exhausted.

name: kernel.ir_op_priority.rms_norm
description: Priority list for vllm.ir.ops.rms_norm

name: kernel.ir_op_priority.fused_add_rms_norm
description: Priority list for vllm.ir.ops.fused_add_rms_norm

name: kernel.ir_op_priority.gelu_and_mul_sparse
description: Priority list for vllm.ir.ops.gelu_and_mul_sparse

name: kernel.enable_flashinfer_autotune
description: If True, run FlashInfer autotuning during kernel warmup.

name: kernel.enable_cutedsl_warmup
description: Deprecated: run legacy CuTeDSL warmup providers.

name: kernel.enable_jit_warmup
description: If True, run JIT compile warmup during kernel warmup.

name: kernel.moe_backend
description: Backend for MoE expert computation kernels.

name: kernel.sparse_indexer_topk_backend
description: Backend for the DSA sparse indexer decode top-k kernel.

name: kernel.linear_backend
description: Backend for linear layer GEMM kernels. Available options: Layer types without an implementation from the requested backend use automatic selection.

name: kernel.linear_backend_per_quant
description: Backend overrides keyed by linear quantization scheme. Overrides take precedence over ``linear_backend``; for example, ``{"nvfp4_w4a16": "humming"}``.

name: structured_outputs.backend
description: Which engine will be used for structured outputs (e.g. JSON schema, regex, etc) by default. With "auto", we will make opinionated choices based on request contents and what the backend libraries currently support, so the behavior is subject to change in each release.

name: structured_outputs.disable_any_whitespace
description: If `True`, json output will always be compact without any whitespace. If `False`, the model may generate whitespace between JSON fields, which is still valid JSON. This is only supported for xgrammar and guidance backends.

name: structured_outputs.disable_additional_properties
description: If `True`, the `guidance` backend will not use `additionalProperties` in the JSON schema. This is only supported for the `guidance` backend and is used to better align its behaviour with `outlines` and `xgrammar`.

name: structured_outputs.reasoning_parser
description: Select the reasoning parser depending on the model that you're using. This is used to parse the reasoning content into OpenAI API format.

name: structured_outputs.reasoning_parser_plugin
description: Path to a dynamically reasoning parser plugin that can be dynamically loaded and registered.

name: structured_outputs.enable_in_reasoning
description: Whether to use structured input for reasoning.

name: profiler.profiler
description: Which profiler to use. Defaults to None. Options are: - 'torch': Use PyTorch profiler. - 'cuda': Use CUDA profiler. - 'proton': Use Triton Proton profiler.

name: profiler.torch_profiler_dir
description: Directory to save torch profiler traces. Both AsyncLLM's CPU traces and worker's traces (CPU & GPU) will be saved under this directory. Note that it must be an absolute path.

name: profiler.proton_profiler_dir
description: Directory to save Triton Proton profiles. Each worker writes a separate rank-qualified file.

name: profiler.proton_context
description: Proton context source. ``shadow`` records explicit scopes with low overhead; ``python`` records Python call stacks.

name: profiler.proton_data
description: Proton output type. ``tree`` produces Hatchet data and ``trace`` produces a Chrome trace.

name: profiler.proton_backend
description: Proton GPU backend. ``None`` lets Proton select CUPTI automatically.

name: profiler.proton_mode
description: Optional backend-specific Proton mode string, such as ``pcsampling``.

name: profiler.proton_hook
description: Optional Proton hook. Use ``triton`` to add Triton launch metadata.

name: profiler.proton_output_format
description: Optional format passed to Proton when finalizing a profile. ``None`` uses the default format for ``proton_data``.

name: profiler.proton_graph_attribution
description: Observe CUDA graph capture so replayed kernels can be attributed. Requires Triton >= 3.7 and ``proton_data='tree'``.

name: profiler.torch_profiler_with_stack
description: If `True`, enables stack tracing in the torch profiler. Enabled by default as it is useful for debugging. Can be disabled via --profiler-config.torch_profiler_with_stack=false CLI flag.

name: profiler.torch_profiler_with_flops
description: If `True`, enables FLOPS counting in the torch profiler. Disabled by default.

name: profiler.torch_profiler_use_gzip
description: If `True`, saves torch profiler traces in gzip format. Enabled by default

name: profiler.torch_profiler_dump_cuda_time_total
description: If `True`, dumps total CUDA time in torch profiler traces. Enabled by default.

name: profiler.torch_profiler_record_shapes
description: If `True`, records tensor shapes in the torch profiler. Disabled by default.

name: profiler.torch_profiler_with_memory
description: If `True`, enables memory profiling in the torch profiler. Disabled by default.

name: profiler.capture_torch_profiler
description: If `True`, enables a torch profiler during CUDA graph capture on rank 0. Traces are saved to a `capture_traces` subdirectory under `torch_profiler_dir`. Requires `profiler` to be set to 'torch'.

name: profiler.detailed_trace_annotation
description: If `True`, uses detailed annotations with roofline metrics (sk, sqsq, sqsk) in profiler trace events. If `False`, uses simple annotations with only context/generation request counts and token counts. Disabled by default.

name: profiler.ignore_frontend
description: If `True`, disables the front-end profiling of AsyncLLM when using the 'torch' profiler. This is needed to reduce overhead when using delay/limit options, since the front-end profiling does not track iterations and will capture the entire range.

name: profiler.delay_iterations
description: Number of engine iterations to skip before starting profiling. Defaults to 0, meaning profiling starts immediately after receiving /start_profile.

name: profiler.max_iterations
description: Maximum number of engine iterations to profile after starting profiling. Defaults to 0, meaning no limit.

name: profiler.warmup_iterations
description: Number of warmup iterations for PyTorch profiler schedule. During warmup, the profiler runs but data is discarded. This helps reduce noise from JIT compilation and other one-time costs in the profiled trace. Defaults to 0 (schedule-based profiling disabled, recording all iterations).

name: profiler.active_iterations
description: Number of active iterations for PyTorch profiler schedule. This is the number of iterations where profiling data is actually collected. Defaults to 5 active iterations.

name: profiler.wait_iterations
description: Number of wait iterations for PyTorch profiler schedule. During wait, the profiler is completely off with zero overhead. This allows skipping initial iterations before warmup begins. Defaults to 0 (no wait period).

name: weight_transfer.backend
description: The backend to use for weight transfer. Validated against the `WeightTransferEngineFactory` registry at engine creation time.
